newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends little changed in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends little changed in slow trade.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended little changed on Tuesday, as extremely slow trade reflected market uncertainties with the London Metal Exchange closed on Monday for a bank holiday, traders said.
The most actively traded August 1997 contract ended at an intraday low of 23,500 yuan ($2,833) per tonne, losing 40 yuan. It opened at 23,500 and hit a high of 23,560 yuan per tonne.
May was unchanged at 23,400 yuan and June flat at 23,500, July edged down 40 yuan to 23,500, September was unchanged at 23,480 and October dropped 30 to 23,400 yuan.
Combined volume fell sharply to 9,610 tonnes from 17,210.
Copper opened little changed and moved around opening levels for most of the session.
Traders said many investors stayed on the sidelines due to a lack of market-moving news.
"Investors are mixed about what direction the market will take and most of them prefer to wait and see," one trader said.
"Another factor is that the bullish stock markets are attracting most investors' attention," he said.
Shanghai's A shares continued their strong run of the past few months on Tuesday, ending up 2.38 percent at 1,549.372 points on a two-year high turnover of 15.7 billion yuan.
The price of physical copper in the Shanghai area is around 23,300/500 yuan per tonne, traders said.
Traders said they expected copper to continue moving around current levels in the short term, as long as market-moving news is thin on the ground.
Aluminium ended down across the board. May fell 100 yuan to 15,300, June 20 to 15,580 and July 50 to 15,700 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 180 tonnes from 320 tonnes.
